summary: Wave 3 Phase B (increment 1) backend testing complete. Ran 19 pytest cases covering GET /api/search (public, driver, customer, admin, malformed JWT, scope=marketing) and GET /api/driver/dashboard (schema + RBAC for driver/customer/admin), plus regression checks for auth/login, catalog endpoints, admin/stats and jobs/nearby. ALL 19 TESTS PASSED. However, a critical code review uncovered two real bugs in the driver dashboard aggregation that the schema-only tests do not catch: it queries the wrong collection/field names, so review-based rating and documents-verification counts are always empty for drivers. Reporting to main agent for a fix.

critical.issue: Bug in review lookup: server.py:2170 queries db.reviews with {'driver_id': user['id']} but reviews are stored with 'target_id' (see server.py:1357 & 1367). As a result the dashboard's user.rating always falls back to the stored value and user.review_count is always 0 regardless of how many reviews the driver has received.

Bug in documents lookup: server.py:2177 queries db.driver_documents but driver uploads are actually inserted into db.documents (see server.py:549). Consequently verification.docs_verified / docs_pending / docs_rejected are always 0 on the dashboard, even when the driver has uploaded/approved docs.

minor.issue: Week-start calc (server.py:2105) uses `start_day.replace(day=start_day.day - start_day.weekday())`. This raises ValueError when the current day-of-month is less than or equal to the weekday index (e.g. Tue 1st of a month => day=0). Use `start_day - timedelta(days=start_day.weekday())` instead.

action_items: Fix server.py:2170 — change `{'driver_id': user['id']}` to `{'target_id': user['id']}` so driver rating & review_count reflect real reviews.
Fix server.py:2177 — change collection name from `db.driver_documents` to `db.documents` so verification counts on the dashboard aggregate real driver documents.
Fix server.py:2105 week-start calc to use `start_day - timedelta(days=start_day.weekday())` to avoid ValueError near month boundaries.
Consider adding an integration-style test that seeds a review + driver doc for driver1 and asserts these fields propagate through /api/driver/dashboard.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 2719 lines — continues to grow; consider splitting driver/admin/search routes into their own modules (search_service.py is already a good start).
/api/search uses regex over 7+ text fields on every query with $or; add MongoDB text indexes on jobs.title/description/pickup_town/dropoff_town/category to keep this performant at scale.
In /api/search the users lookup regex is also applied to `id` (UUID) which will only match if the query is a UUID substring — fine but worth noting.
Driver dashboard bookings query does not project fields; on large drivers this will load all booking fields into memory (500 doc cap). Consider a projection.
seed_data_creation: No new seed data created. Used existing seeded users (admin@cargoone.com, driver1@cargoone.com, cust1@cargoone.com).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Existing pytest file at /app/backend/tests/test_wave3_phaseB_search_and_driver_dashboard.py covers /api/search & /api/driver/dashboard. After the two collection/field fixes on driver dashboard, add an assertion that verifies review_count and verification.docs_verified reflect seeded data. BASE_URL resolved via EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (frontend/.env sets that; EXPO_BACKEND_URL is not set in this environment).
rca_of_issue: Two mismatched collection/field names in /api/driver/dashboard: (1) reviews are inserted with target_id but the dashboard filters by driver_id, so it never finds them; (2) documents are inserted into db.documents but the dashboard reads db.driver_documents, so all verification counts stay at 0. Root cause: aggregation code was written against a different naming convention than the rest of the codebase. Reproduction: log in as driver1, approve their docs via admin, complete a booking + leave a review targeting driver1, then GET /api/driver/dashboard — user.review_count and verification.docs_verified will still be 0. Mitigation: update the two queries to use the correct collection and field names.
